trigger.label: Trigger – Vendor Email
trigger.title: Incoming Service Invoice Email
bullets: A vendor sends an email containing the service invoice (PDF, scanned image, or XML) to a dedicated, monitored mailbox.
The Orchestrator Agent continuously scans this inbox via Microsoft Graph API / Outlook Connector / IMAP.
On detection of a new email with attachment(s), the agent captures:
Email Metadata: From (vendor email address), Subject (typical invoice subject), Date.
Attachments: All invoice files and any supporting documents (e.g., delivery notes, SES approval).
A unique Global Service Invoice ID is generated for end-to-end traceability, e.g.: SERV-INV-20260511-784512.
The original email and attachments are securely archived, and the payload is handed off to the Extractor Agent.

orchestrator.label: Orchestrator Agent
orchestrator.title: Central Process Coordinator
bullets: Acts as the brain and traffic controller of the entire invoice processing pipeline.
Key Responsibilities:
Assigns the Global Service Invoice ID.
Logs all events to the central audit trail.
Routes the invoice package (email + attachments) to the next agent.
Identifies the correct target ERP system (SAP S/4HANA or Dynamics 365 BC) based on Company Code / PO prefix.
Maintains the state of each invoice (Received, In Extraction, Validating, Posting, Completed).
Provides real-time status updates to the monitoring dashboard.
Ensures that every handover between agents is asynchronous and reliable, eliminating manual inbox sorting.

extractor.label: Service PO Extractor Agent
extractor.title: Intelligent Document Extraction
bullets: Receives the raw email and attachment(s) from the Orchestrator.
Processing Steps:
Detects file type (PDF, image, XML).
Applies OCR (Optical Character Recognition) combined with AI Document Intelligence (e.g., Azure Form Recognizer / NA10) to read the invoice.
Handles multi-page invoices, complex line-item tables, and handwritten or scanned content.
Extracts Critical Data Fields:
Header: Vendor Name/Code, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, Purchase Order Number, Service Entry Sheet number (if present), Currency, Total Amount.
Line Items: Service Description, Service Number, Quantity, Unit of Measure, Unit Rate, Line Amount, Account Assignment hints (Cost Center, WBS, Project).
Tax & Banking: Tax details, Payment Due Date, Bank account information.
Quality Control:
A confidence score (0–100%) is assigned to each extracted field and an overall document score.
In the ideal flow, all fields exceed the pre-set threshold (e.g., 85%), and the data is packaged as a structured JSON payload.
The final payload, together with the original document link, is passed to the Translator Agent.

translator.label: Service PO Translator Agent
translator.title: Data Normalisation & Standardisation
bullets: The Translator Agent ensures that extracted data matches the ERP system’s language and formats.
Normalisation Actions:
Language Translation: Converts invoice text to the required language (if multi-lingual extraction occurred).

Currency & UoM Conversion: Aligns currencies and units of measure with the company code’s master data (e.g., convert foreign currency to local currency using the latest exchange rate; map “hour” to “HRS”).
Tax Code Standardisation: Maps textual tax descriptions to system tax codes. For example, “VAT 12%” becomes the SAP tax code UZ_VAT12, or the corresponding D365 BC tax code.
Field Formatting: Dates are converted to the ERP-expected format (YYYY-MM-DD), vendor codes are matched to the master record, and PO numbers are normalised (removing spaces/special characters).
The normalised, clean data payload is then ready for compliance verification.

compliance.label: Compliance Checker Agent + Master Data Agent
compliance.title: Multi-Layered Business & Master Data Validation
bullets: The Service Master Data Agent fetches live master records from SAP / D365 BC for validation.
The Compliance Checker Agent runs layered checks with clear pass/fail outcomes:

Vendor Validation: Vendor exists and is active in the relevant Company Code; vendor is not blocked for posting/payment; bank account details match the master record (fraud prevention); Tax ID / GSTIN / PINFL matches the vendor master.
Regulatory & Policy Compliance: Applies country-specific rules (e.g., Uzbekistan VAT, India GST); checks for any mandatory withholding tax applicability on services.

Document Completeness: PO number is present and valid in the system; service lines are properly identified (Item Category “D” in SAP or Resource lines in BC); relevant supporting documents are referenced.
Duplicate Invoice Check: Searches across both SAP and BC using Vendor + Invoice No. + Date + Amount; prevents accidental double-posting.
Successful Outcome: All checks pass → the invoice moves forward to the Validation Agent.
In this clean demo, no business exceptions occur, ensuring a straight-through processing path.

validation.label: Service Validation Agent
validation.title: Three-Way Match & Tolerance Enforcement
bullets: The Validation Agent performs the three-way match, the core control for service procurement.

For SAP Environments: Retrieves the Purchase Order (ME23N) and verifies Item Category = D (Services); checks the Service Entry Sheet (SES) status in ML81N – must be “Accepted”; compares Invoice lines vs. Accepted SES quantities/amounts vs. PO lines.

For Dynamics 365 Business Central: Retrieves the Purchase Order and ensures a Posted Purchase Receipt exists for the resource/service lines; compares Invoice Qty/Cost vs. Received Qty/Cost on the receipt.
Tolerance Check: Applies configured tolerances for price, quantity, and amount (SAP OMR6 / LIV; BC Purchases & Payables Setup).
Exact matches or small variances within tolerance → auto-approved.
Validation Output: A verified, tolerance-compliant invoice ready for final posting.

posting.label: Service Posting Agent
posting.title: Final Enrichment & System Posting
bullets: The Posting Agent receives the approved payload and performs the final ERP booking.

Pre-Posting Enrichment: Pulls the latest account assignment data (Cost Center, WBS Element, Internal Order) from the master records; applies the correct tax codes and G/L accounts based on automatic account determination (OBYC in SAP, Posting Groups in BC).
System-Specific Posting Actions:

SAP S/4HANA: Utilises BAPI_INCOMINGINVOICE_CREATE (or an IDoc INVOIC01) to simulate the MIRO transaction in the background; references the Purchase Order Number and Accepted Service Entry Sheet; posts the invoice, generating an Invoice Receipt (IR) in PO history; produces an SAP Invoice Document Number (e.g., 5100000123).

Dynamics 365 BC: Creates a Purchase Invoice via API / Web Service; uses Get Receipt Lines (if receipt-based matching is enabled) to fetch the goods receipt; posts the Purchase Invoice, updating PO status and creating a Vendor Ledger Entry.

Post-Posting Actions: Creates an open vendor item in Accounts Payable; triggers a Payment Proposal Run automatically (F110 in SAP / Payment Journal in BC) if the payment due date is met; sends a confirmation email to the AP team and the vendor (optional).

completion.label: Completion – Invoice Posted
completion.title: Finalisation & Audit Trail Update
bullets: The Global Service Invoice ID is marked as “Completed” in the audit log.
Key Outcomes:
The posted document number (SAP Invoice Doc No. or BC Posted Invoice No.) is linked to the original Global ID for full traceability.
The central dashboard updates the invoice status and triggers any required alerts.
All actions are recorded in the Agentic AI Operations Audit Log, ensuring a transparent, compliant process.
The end-to-end journey – from vendor email to posted invoice – is now fully automated, fully visible, and free of manual intervention.
